_doc: 2024-2026 crop-recommendation papers. Every DOI/arXiv id checked against Crossref/arXiv (2026-11-23); every quote checked against the publisher full text. Gap codes: KAGGLE_ONLY, RANDOM_SPLIT_ONLY, NO_YIELD, NO_UNCERTAINTY, SINGLE_REGION, NO_STAT_TEST, LEAKAGE, NOT_REPRODUCIBLE. 'ref' = number in docs/research/LITERATURE.md / references.bib. AgroMind numbers in gap_text come from docs/research/results.json v4.numbers.

papers.title: Machine learning based recommendation of agricultural and horticultural crop farming in India under the regime of NPK, soil pH and three climatic variables
papers.dataset: Kaggle crop set (paper: 2,100 points, 11 agricultural + 10 horticultural crops; N, P, K, pH, rainfall, temperature, humidity)
papers.method: XGBoost, SVM, RF, KNN, DT; separate models for agricultural, horticultural and combined crops
papers.method_quote: the learning rate was set to 0.1, max depth to 17, n estimators to 200, subsample rate was set to 0.5, gamma value was set to 0, and the seed was set to 50 (Sec 2.2.2)
papers.metric_quote: XGBoost demonstrated the highest test accuracy of 99.09 % and KNN demonstrated the lowest test accuracy of 94.45 % for agricultural crops. (Sec 3.2, Table 1)
papers.protocol: single random 70/30 split; under-sampling (order vs split not stated)
papers.protocol_quote: The training dataset consisted of 70 % of the available data, while the remaining 30 % was reserved for testing purposes. (Sec 2.3)
papers.availability: Data will be made available on request.
papers.gap_text: One random split of the Kaggle table with no location or year, so 99% says nothing about a new state. What we do instead: on the Kaggle 2,200-row set a plain Random Forest already scores 99.5% on a random split (v4.numbers KaggleRF); our v4 test holds out whole Indian states (43,443 DES district-season-years): literature classifiers fall to 36.3% (RF) / 38.2% (XGBoost) hit@1 for the best-yielding crop, versus 57.5% / 57.5% on a random split; YieldRank reaches 55.6% (v4.numbers RFHitLSO, XGBHitLSO, RFHitR, XGBHitR, OursHitLSO); we give 90% conformal crop shortlists that cover 90.1% on unseen states with 2.87 crops on average (v4.numbers CovIIDLSO, SizeIIDLSO).

reimplement.name: Dey2024-XGB (+SVM/RF/KNN/DT)

papers.title: A Decision Support System for Crop Recommendation Using Machine Learning Classification Algorithms
papers.dataset: own records from agriculture offices + farmer interviews, three Odisha districts (Koraput, Gajapati, Rayagada)
papers.method: 13 classifiers (LR, DT, KNN, SVC, RF, GB, Bagging, XGB, AdaBoost, CatBoost, HGB, SGD, MNB) before and after SMOTE
papers.method_quote: we have applied 13 different methods such as logistic regression, decision tree, K-Neighbors, SVC, random forest, Gradient Boosting, bagging tree, XGB Classifier, Ada Boost Classifier, Cat Boost, HGB, SGDC, and MNB. (Sec 3.17.2) -- no hyper-parameters stated
papers.reported_value: 1.0 (SGD classifier after SMOTE; SVC 1.0 before SMOTE)
papers.metric_quote: after the SMOTE ... the accuracy of the SVC is reduced to 0.74 and XGBoost to 0.97, and the SGDC is improved to 1.0. (Conclusion; Tables 3-6)
papers.protocol_quote: we trained for 80% of the dataset using these classifiers and tested for 20% of the data.
papers.availability: available from the corresponding author upon reasonable request
papers.gap_text: Real Indian records, but three districts, one random split, and accuracy of 1.0 that cannot be checked because data and settings are not public. What we do instead: our v4 test holds out whole Indian states (43,443 DES district-season-years): literature classifiers fall to 36.3% (RF) / 38.2% (XGBoost) hit@1 for the best-yielding crop, versus 57.5% / 57.5% on a random split; YieldRank reaches 55.6% (v4.numbers RFHitLSO, XGBHitLSO, RFHitR, XGBHitR, OursHitLSO); we give 90% conformal crop shortlists that cover 90.1% on unseen states with 2.87 crops on average (v4.numbers CovIIDLSO, SizeIIDLSO).

papers.title: Crop recommendation with machine learning: leveraging environmental and economic factors for optimal crop selection
papers.dataset: Kaggle crop-yield table (vihith12) merged with DES cost of cultivation and MSP; 19 crops, 15 states, 2011-14
papers.method: Random Forest and SVM in R; 10-fold CV vs chronological split vs lag features (lags: Year 5, Season 7)
papers.method_quote: the number of lags for the variable Year was set to 5 while the number of lags for the variable Season was set to 7 (Sec 3.2.3) -- RF/SVM settings not stated
papers.metric_quote: 10-fold cross validation approach produced exceptionally high accuracy (RF: 99.96%, SVM: 94.71%) ... reduces the model performance (RF: 78.55%, SVM: 71.18%) in the Time-series Split approach (Abstract)
papers.protocol: random 10-fold CV and an 80/20 chronological split; no spatial hold-out
papers.protocol_quote: the developed models were trained using the data from past years (2011-14) and the test data mostly included instances from the year 2014.
papers.availability: data from Kaggle, DES and Farmer's Portal (links given); no code
papers.gap_text: The only paper with a time-ordered test, but every state is in both train and test and yield was dropped as a variable. What we do instead: our v4 test holds out whole Indian states (43,443 DES district-season-years): literature classifiers fall to 36.3% (RF) / 38.2% (XGBoost) hit@1 for the best-yielding crop, versus 57.5% / 57.5% on a random split; YieldRank reaches 55.6% (v4.numbers RFHitLSO, XGBHitLSO, RFHitR, XGBHitR, OursHitLSO); we give 90% conformal crop shortlists that cover 90.1% on unseen states with 2.87 crops on average (v4.numbers CovIIDLSO, SizeIIDLSO).

papers.title: High-precision crop recommendation system with stacking ensemble classifiers for optimizing agricultural productivity
papers.dataset: Kaggle crop set (2,200 rows, 22 crops); second set FAO (28,242 rows)
papers.method: two stacking ensembles (KNN+RF+NB -> LR; KNN+Bagging+NB -> LR) and a hard-voting ensemble (LR, XGB, RF, DT, GNB); PCA+MI+RFE feature fusion
papers.method_quote: three foundational models, KNN, Bagging, and NB, are combined at the primary level. Similarly, the LR model is employed at the second level (Experimental study) -- base-learner hyper-parameters not stated
papers.reported_value: up to 99.56% (abstract); Table 2: 99.54% second stacking, 99.09% voting; FAO set 85.6%
papers.metric_quote: the voting ensemble classifier proved to be the most effective, when applied to the first small dataset, achieving an impressive accuracy up to 99.56%. (Abstract)
papers.protocol_quote: allocating 80% of the dataset for training and the remaining 20% for testing.
papers.availability: All data are available upon request from the corresponding author.
papers.gap_text: Abstract, text and Table 2 give three different headline accuracies (99.56 / 99.53 / 99.09%) for the same Kaggle task. What we do instead: on the Kaggle 2,200-row set a plain Random Forest already scores 99.5% on a random split (v4.numbers KaggleRF); our v4 test holds out whole Indian states (43,443 DES district-season-years): literature classifiers fall to 36.3% (RF) / 38.2% (XGBoost) hit@1 for the best-yielding crop, versus 57.5% / 57.5% on a random split; YieldRank reaches 55.6% (v4.numbers RFHitLSO, XGBHitLSO, RFHitR, XGBHitR, OursHitLSO); we give 90% conformal crop shortlists that cover 90.1% on unseen states with 2.87 crops on average (v4.numbers CovIIDLSO, SizeIIDLSO).

papers.dataset: Kaggle crop set, 2,200 rows, 22 crops (authors attribute it to Islamabad stations)

papers.metric_quote: RFXG concept achieves 98% accuracy, precision, recall, and F1 scoring.

papers.availability: The datasets can be requested from Hadeeqa Afzal.
papers.gap_text: A Random Forest with only 2 trees already reaches 96% precision, recall and F1 ('RF achieves 96% precision, 96% recall, and 96% F1'), which shows how easy the Kaggle task is. What we do instead: on the Kaggle 2,200-row set a plain Random Forest already scores 99.5% on a random split (v4.numbers KaggleRF); our v4 test holds out whole Indian states (43,443 DES district-season-years): literature classifiers fall to 36.3% (RF) / 38.2% (XGBoost) hit@1 for the best-yielding crop, versus 57.5% / 57.5% on a random split; YieldRank reaches 55.6% (v4.numbers RFHitLSO, XGBHitLSO, RFHitR, XGBHitR, OursHitLSO); we give 90% conformal crop shortlists that cover 90.1% on unseen states with 2.87 crops on average (v4.numbers CovIIDLSO, SizeIIDLSO).

What we do instead: on the Kaggle 2,200-row set a plain Random Forest already scores 99.5% on a random split (v4.numbers KaggleRF); our v4 test holds out whole Indian states (43,443 DES district-season-years): literature classifiers fall to 36.3% (RF) / 38.2% (XGBoost) hit@1 for the best-yielding crop, versus 57.5% / 57.5% on a random split; YieldRank reaches 55.6% (v4.numbers RFHitLSO, XGBHitLSO, RFHitR, XGBHitR, OursHitLSO); we give 90% conformal crop shortlists that cover 90.1% on unseen states with 2.87 crops on average (v4.numbers CovIIDLSO, SizeIIDLSO).

papers.title: Enhancing precision agriculture through cloud based transformative crop recommendation model
papers.dataset: unnamed table, 3,000 rows x 8 columns (N, P, K, temperature, humidity, pH, rainfall, crop)
papers.region: Punjab framing; data source not named
papers.method: TCRM: RF + Extra Trees fused with a Keras network (dense, normalisation, multi-head attention)
papers.method_quote: the number of estimators (trees) in a model is commonly between 100 and 500 ... In attention-based models, you can mention the number of heads, e.g., 4 or 8. -- only ranges, final values not stated

papers.title: Physics-Aware Ensemble Learning for Superior Crop Recommendation in Smart Agriculture
papers.method: stacking (RF, Extra Trees, XGBoost -> LR) tuned by GridSearch/RandomSearch/Optuna, plus a physics-informed NN penalising implausible temperature/pH
papers.method_quote: Table 3 (Optuna): RF max_depth: 16, min_samples_split: 10, n_estimators: 116 | Extra Tree max_depth: 16, min_samples_split: 5, n_estimators: 441 | XGBoost learning_rate: 0.0640, max_depth: 7, n_estimators: 465 | LR C: 829.97, penalty: l2; Sec 3.3: fixed random seed (42), 5-fold stratified CV
papers.metric_quote: achieving an accuracy of 0.9950 ± 0.0017, precision of 0.9952 ± 0.0016, and recall of 0.9950 ± 0.0017 across five-fold cross-validation (Sec 6)
papers.protocol_quote: The preprocessed data is then divided into training and testing datasets of 80% and 20%, respectively ... we then used 5-fold stratified cross-validation. (Sec 3.3)
papers.gap_text: Best-documented Kaggle stack, but the physics penalty uses each crop's ideal temperature and pH, which is close to the label itself. What we do instead: on the Kaggle 2,200-row set a plain Random Forest already scores 99.5% on a random split (v4.numbers KaggleRF); our v4 test holds out whole Indian states (43,443 DES district-season-years): literature classifiers fall to 36.3% (RF) / 38.2% (XGBoost) hit@1 for the best-yielding crop, versus 57.5% / 57.5% on a random split; YieldRank reaches 55.6% (v4.numbers RFHitLSO, XGBHitLSO, RFHitR, XGBHitR, OursHitLSO); we give 90% conformal crop shortlists that cover 90.1% on unseen states with 2.87 crops on average (v4.numbers CovIIDLSO, SizeIIDLSO).

papers.title: An explainable spatio-temporal deep learning framework for crop yield prediction and recommendation
papers.dataset: Kaggle crop set (2,200 rows) + Kaggle FAO yield table (1990-2016, multi-country), merged
papers.method: PO-STX-GTNET (conv + Transformer encoder + BiGRU + attention, tuned by a PantheraCobra optimiser); HK-ELM-A for yield
papers.method_quote: trained using the Adam optimizer with an initial learning rate of 0.001 ... batch sizes ranging from 32 to 128 ... epochs varies between 50 and 200 -- final values not stated

papers.title: A crop recommendation using improved expert-guided constraint aware differential evolution and CatBoost surrogate learning
papers.dataset: Mendeley Tamil Nadu district crop-suitability table (3,437 rows, 37 districts, 105 crops), expanded to 381,507 scenario rows
papers.method: expert suitability score optimised by improved differential evolution; CatBoost regressor as surrogate
papers.method_quote: | CatBoost iterations | 300 | CatBoost tree depth | 6 | CatBoost learning rate | 0.05 | (Table 3)
papers.reported_metric: R2 of surrogate vs expert score
papers.metric_quote: coefficient of determination (R 2) = 0.9975, Mean Absolute Error (MAE) = 0.0043, and Root Mean Square Error (RMSE) = 0.0056
papers.protocol: random 80/20 split of generated rows + 5-fold CV
papers.protocol_quote: The created surrogate dataset was divided in the ratio of 80:20 for training and testing purposes
papers.availability: data on Mendeley (link given); no code
papers.gap_text: The model imitates a hand-made scoring formula ('trained to mimic the deterministic expert-defined suitability scoring function'), so R2 0.9975 is fidelity to a formula, not to farm outcomes. What we do instead: our v4 test holds out whole Indian states (43,443 DES district-season-years): literature classifiers fall to 36.3% (RF) / 38.2% (XGBoost) hit@1 for the best-yielding crop, versus 57.5% / 57.5% on a random split; YieldRank reaches 55.6% (v4.numbers RFHitLSO, XGBHitLSO, RFHitR, XGBHitR, OursHitLSO); we give 90% conformal crop shortlists that cover 90.1% on unseen states with 2.87 crops on average (v4.numbers CovIIDLSO, SizeIIDLSO).

papers.title: AgriOptNet: A hybrid optimization and lightweight deep learning framework for soil texture classification and crop recommendation based on nutrition

papers.metric_quote: The system performance decreases to Accuracy 0.9824 and F1 0.9723 when 250 m spatial blocks (SB-CV) spatial structure becomes the basis

papers.title: AgroSense 2.0: Cross-Modal Transformer Fusion with Geospatial Raster Integration and Interpretable Multi-Task Learning for Precision Crop Recommendation
papers.dataset: Kaggle-style 7-feature, 22-crop table + soil images + India soil raster (not geo-paired)
papers.region: India raster; tabular rows have no location
papers.method: EfficientNet-B0 + tabular encoder fused by 8-head cross-attention, multi-task (crop + soil); LightGBM baseline
papers.method_quote: We use AdamW with weight decay η = 0.01 and initial learning rate α0 = 3 × 10^-4 ... Training proceeds for 15 epochs with batch size 32. (Sec 3.3)
papers.metric_quote: The full AgroSense 2.0 model achieves 99.3% test accuracy with macro F1 of 99.1%, outperforming all baselines including the strong tabular-only LightGBM.
papers.protocol_quote: The dataset is partitioned using stratified sampling at an 80/10/10 train/validation/test ratio
papers.availability: no code or data link found
papers.gap_text: Images are paired with table rows by index ('tab_idx = i mod |D_tab|'), not by place, and the 0.2-point gain over LightGBM sits on a saturated benchmark. What we do instead: on the Kaggle 2,200-row set a plain Random Forest already scores 99.5% on a random split (v4.numbers KaggleRF); our v4 test holds out whole Indian states (43,443 DES district-season-years): literature classifiers fall to 36.3% (RF) / 38.2% (XGBoost) hit@1 for the best-yielding crop, versus 57.5% / 57.5% on a random split; YieldRank reaches 55.6% (v4.numbers RFHitLSO, XGBHitLSO, RFHitR, XGBHitR, OursHitLSO); we give 90% conformal crop shortlists that cover 90.1% on unseen states with 2.87 crops on average (v4.numbers CovIIDLSO, SizeIIDLSO).
